apps.name: Notes
apps.summary: Write, save and export a note. A quiet page on your server.
implementation: Installs a small Notes web app at /apps/notes/.
Runs inside your existing website server, using no additional server slot.
Your edits stay in browser storage. Export text to keep or share a copy.

apps.name: Task Board
apps.summary: Turn an idea into tasks. Move work from to do to done.
implementation: Installs a three-column task board at /apps/task-board/.
Shares the server you select; its actual files count toward your disk allowance.
Tasks stay in this browser. Export the board as JSON for a portable copy.

apps.name: JSON Studio
apps.summary: Validate, format and export JSON right in your browser.
implementation: Installs a browser-based data editor at /apps/json-studio/.
Validates JSON locally; no document is sent to a provider or API.
Uses only its small app files on the server. Your document stays in this browser.

apps.name: Pixel Canvas
apps.summary: Draw in our pink, white and blue. Export your own pixel art.
implementation: Installs a 16 × 16 drawing app at /apps/pixel-canvas/.
Paint with NUCALORIC colors using a mouse, touch or keyboard.
Exports a 512 × 512 PNG. Your drawing stays in this browser.

apps.name: Solana
apps.summary: The chain underneath your coin and wallet.
implementation: Read chain state, simulate transactions, and confirm user-signed transactions.
Public RPC can be read without an account; production RPC capacity must be provisioned.
A devnet transaction is simulated, approved in a real wallet, submitted, and confirmed; commitment, retries, and RPC limits are handled.

apps.name: Helius
apps.summary: RPC access and chain data for your app.
implementation: Production RPC and indexed chain data for launch and market workflows.
Create an account and provision an RPC endpoint or API key under the chosen plan.
Authenticated RPC reads, quota handling, and independent health checks work; endpoint secrets stay on the server.

apps.name: Phantom
apps.summary: A wallet for your Solana identity.
implementation: Wallet connection and user-approved Solana transaction signing.
A compatible wallet and explicit user connection/signing consent.
Real connect, rejection, disconnect, network mismatch, and signing flows pass on devnet.

apps.name: Solflare
apps.summary: Connect a Solana wallet to your work.
implementation: An additional Solana wallet option.
Use the official wallet integration documentation and user signing consent.
Wallet detection, connection, cancellation, and devnet signing work on supported devices.

apps.name: Backpack
apps.summary: Keep a wallet close to your project.
implementation: An additional wallet option for project creators.
Use the wallet provider integration and user connection/signing consent.
Provider availability, rejection, disconnect, and devnet transaction signing pass.

apps.name: Meteora
apps.summary: Liquidity tools for a coin with a plan.
implementation: Dynamic Bonding Curve launch configuration and a planned liquidity migration path.
Official SDKs are public; chain operations require RPC capacity, a wallet, and transaction fees.
Devnet create/swap/migrate tests pass with validated parameters and explicit signing; fee and migration behavior are documented.

apps.name: Jupiter
apps.summary: Token discovery and wallet-approved swaps.
implementation: Price discovery and a reviewed swap-routing integration.
Create a developer-platform key and confirm the API family, plan, and quotas.
Quotes are fresh, token mints verified, slippage bounded, and signed execution confirmed on chain.

apps.name: Raydium
apps.summary: Solana pools and liquidity tooling.
implementation: Alternative launch and liquidity research; route selection remains a design decision.
Review official SDK/program references; transactions require wallet signing and RPC.
One explicit launch route is chosen; program/configuration and fee behavior are verified in integration tests.

apps.name: Birdeye
apps.summary: Another view of token and market data.
implementation: Token market data and freshness checks for discovery.
Confirm endpoint access and API-key requirements with the developer portal; several deep documentation links were unavailable during this review.
Authorized reads, timestamp validation, rate limits, and unavailable-data UI work.

apps.name: Paymenter
apps.summary: The account and billing home for your servers.
implementation: Orders, invoices, and service state for paid developer workspaces.
Deploy your own Paymenter portal; API reference requires v1.2.0+ and a server-side bearer token.
Checkout, paid-order reconciliation, provisioning, suspension, and user ownership checks pass before terminal access is enabled.

apps.name: OpenAI
apps.summary: Bring OpenAI into your next AI workflow.
implementation: A planned Responses/Realtime gateway for project assistants.
Create project access and store an API credential on the backend with usage controls.
Server-side authentication, budgets, streaming errors, cancellation, and tenant boundaries are tested.

apps.name: Claude
apps.summary: A thinking and coding partner from Anthropic.
implementation: A planned Claude model gateway.
Provision Anthropic API access and keep credentials on the backend.
Authenticated requests, quota handling, streaming interruption, and tenant metering pass.

apps.name: Gemini
apps.summary: Google’s models for your next idea.
implementation: A planned Gemini model gateway.
Create the appropriate project/API key and review available quotas.
Server-side access, supported models, quota handling, and tenant metering pass.

apps.name: Grok / xAI
apps.summary: Keep xAI in your AI tool collection.
implementation: A planned Grok model gateway.
Provision xAI API access; it is separate from X social developer credentials.
Authorized server-side calls, streaming failure handling, and budget controls pass.

apps.name: X social API
apps.summary: Plan the community side of your project.
implementation: User-authorized community publishing and project updates.
Approved developer app and an access plan; OAuth mode and scopes depend on the endpoint.
PKCE/user authorization, required scopes, revocation, quotas, and explicit publish consent work.

apps.name: X Money / payments
apps.summary: Keep X Money in your future payment toolkit.
implementation: Conditional future payment rail; not enabled and not interchangeable with independent xMoney products.
Public merchant API access has not been established from official documentation reviewed.
Obtain official merchant eligibility and API documentation first; then review settlement, refunds, and reconciliation.

apps.name: GitHub
apps.summary: Your repositories, close to your workspace.
implementation: Source archive today; planned repository evidence and developer workflow connections.
GitHub CLI is already authorized for this project archive; an in-product integration needs its own authorization.
App/user scopes, project ownership, private repository access, and webhook signature checks are implemented.

apps.name: Cloudflare
apps.summary: A public address and access controls for your app.
implementation: Planned DNS, protected tunnels, edge delivery and storage options for developer projects.
Account, domain and an owner-configured Tunnel/Access policy; credentials remain on the machine or backend.
Verify domain ownership, access policy, tunnel health and revocation before attaching a project.

apps.name: Docker
apps.summary: Containers for work you run on your own machine.
implementation: Planned isolated app containers on a personal PC, Raspberry Pi or managed server.
An owner-managed Linux machine and a supported container engine installation.
Review image architecture, resource limits, non-root permissions, persistent data and restart behavior.

apps.name: Tailscale
apps.summary: A private route between your devices.
implementation: Planned private network access to a developer-owned machine.
An owner-controlled tailnet, enrolled devices and reviewed access policies.
Verify device ownership, least-privilege policy, service reachability and device removal.

apps.name: Raspberry Pi
apps.summary: A small computer for a useful project.
implementation: Planned lightweight ARM workspace on your own hardware.
A developer-owned Raspberry Pi, compatible OS, storage and network connection.
Verify OS/ARM compatibility, resources, explicit enrollment and device heartbeat; a brand status page cannot establish your hardware uptime.

apps.name: Supabase
apps.summary: Database, authentication and storage building blocks.
implementation: Planned project identity, database, storage and application data.
A project with reviewed authentication, database policies and server-side credentials.
Test row-level policies, tenant boundaries, backups and key handling before storing project data.

apps.name: Vercel
apps.summary: A place to deploy and preview a web project.
implementation: Planned app deployment with project previews and build evidence.
An authorized project, repository connection and reviewed build configuration.
Check repository ownership, build results, environment separation and rollback.

apps.name: Netlify
apps.summary: Website delivery and deployment workflows.
implementation: Planned website delivery and deployment previews.
An authorized site, repository connection and reviewed deployment settings.
Check repository ownership, deployment evidence, environment settings and rollback.

apps.name: PostgreSQL
apps.summary: A durable home for your application data.
implementation: Planned durable project data on managed or developer-owned infrastructure.
An owner-managed database with a restricted application role and tested backups.
Test access isolation, migrations, backups and recovery; local database health needs an owner-specific probe.
